::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
The AOS–Chongqing JV (registered April 2016; AOS reported initial capitalisation of $330M and total capitalisation of $379M by November 2019, split 51% AOS / 49% Chongqing funds at formation) that the Wikipedia fab list shows as 'under construction'. It has in fact been in 12-inch mass production since mid-2019. In July 2025 AOS agreed to sell about 20.3% of the JV for $150M to SIMIC Holdings Co., Ltd. (reportedly Shanghai Xinwei Technology Group); the sale completed in May 2026, moving the fab toward Chinese control.
:::

**Chinese name:** 重庆万国半导体科技有限公司 (Chóngqìng Wànguó Bàndǎotǐ Kējì Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

12-inch MOSFET/analog power devices and modules for consumer, industrial and EV-adjacent applications.

## Why does it matter?

A case study in how a US-designed power-semi fab in inland China changes hands without ever closing — the stake sale to a Shanghai tech-asset group mirrors the broader pattern of foreign-origin fabs being absorbed into domestic capital structures.

## Project Timeline

- **Apr 2016** — Company registered in Chongqing Liangjiang New Area (AOS + local state funds)
- **Jun 2018** — Phase-1 fab + assembly/test trial production (20,000 wafers/month)
- **Jul 2019** — 12-inch Phase 1 mass production begins (AOS fiscal Q1 2020, July–September 2019); marketed as China's first integrated 12-inch power fab (company claim)
- **Jul 2025** — AOS agrees to sell 20.3% of the JV (about half its 39.2% stake) for ~$150M to SIMIC Holdings Co., Ltd. (reportedly Shanghai Xinwei); sale completed May 2026
